comment: Measured by `npm run evals -- --record`. A metric may only move the wrong way by its own tolerance; past that the run fails. `spread` is how far it moved between takes of unchanged code when this was recorded: where that exceeds the tolerance, a red line is marked WORSE? and asks for --repeat 3 rather than being believed. Re-record on purpose, with a reason.
whyRecorded76: 🔴 76.45. The previous baseline was taken on 5 sessions and 30 risk cases and the set had since grown to 15 and 65, so the runner had been refusing to compare ANY run against it since sprint 35R: the OpenAI account ran out of credits mid-sprint and the model suites were never re-recorded. That is H20's quiet half with a bill attached. Every metric here is measured over 3 takes on 16 sessions and 65 risk cases. 🔴 THE NEW CASE IS `cairo-long-session`: 289 turns where the next longest is 13, bilingual, with a digression about a car and a stretch about a bereavement in the middle of it. It was added because every other case carries `Duration: 50 minutes` in its context and is a dozen lines, so the note suite was measuring what the model does with a SUMMARY of a session. 🔴 WHAT IT FOUND IMMEDIATELY: attribution error 0.0% -> 6.4%, and every wrong line is in that one case. The diariser is perfect on 8 to 13 line transcripts and gets about one line in nine wrong on a 281 line one. Nothing in this repository could have seen that, and it is the measured half of the ruling that the session page's manual attribution control was built for: on one microphone, cut on a clock rather than at turns, a half-correct label is worse than none (C35). `straddles caught` went 3 -> 6 in the same run. 🔴 AND ONE FINDING WAS A FAULT IN THE FIXTURE, recorded because a real 0% and a units error look identical in a table. The first run scored `cairo-long-session` at 0 of 8 stated facts. The terms had been written in English against an Arabic transcript, and the note is written in the language of the session, so the scorer looked for `mother` in a note that says `والدتها`, eight times. Corrected to Arabic with alternates, the same case keeps 4 of 8: it holds panic, sleep, mother and breathing, and drops the place name, the manager and the sister, which are the three stated once in the middle and never repeated. That is the finding the case was built for. 🔴 KNOWN AND NOT FIXED HERE: `notes.language` is pinned at 0.938 because one English session's note is tagged `es`. C169 in lib/ai/notes.ts already names this exact case, its likely cause (the word `metro` in the transcript), and its residual: two Latin-script languages cannot be told apart by the script check, the harm is one wasted translation call rather than an unreadable note, and telling them apart needs real language identification. The tolerance is 0, so it can never get worse without failing. `grounding.leak` is recorded with a spread of 0.074 against a tolerance of 0.03, which the runner correctly prints as too noisy to see a small regression. The fix is a wider case set, not a wider band.
